note: A field of the wrong JSON type makes the event invalid.
A protocol error names the event type, never the payload.
Member names match exactly: TYPE is not type, so the event has no type.
An object with a duplicate member name is not valid JSON; no implementation merges or picks one.
Names are compared after unescaping.
The whole event is strict JSON, unknown types included.
Only the fields of a consumed type are read, so a future event whose fields share a name with consumed ones is passed through.
An ignored type is not refused for the shape of a field the package does not consume.
A surrogate escape must be a high one followed by a low one.
A surrogate pair escape is one scalar.
One value per message; whitespace may follow it, nothing else.
Whitespace around the value is allowed.
10,000 levels of nesting (the object and 9,999 arrays) are accepted.
10,001 levels are not: Go's jsontext limit, which Swift matches without recursion.
An integer field must fit a signed 64-bit integer.
An integer field is written as an integer: no fraction, no exponent.
The int64 bounds are accepted, and a float that underflows is 0.
A float out of range is refused.
A code that is not a string keeps its exact JSON text.
An object code keeps its exact text, spacing and member order included.
CR and LF are not base64 (Go's decoder would skip them).
Padding only completes the last quantum (Foundation's decoder would accept this).
Standard base64 is padded.
Non-zero trailing bits are ignored, as Go's standard decoder ignores them.
